summary: Describes the end-to-end protocol, block formats, and abstract service for exchanging bundles of messages in Delay Tolerant Networking. It came from the IRTF DTN Research Group and is experimental.

eli5.summary: For places where connections come and go, messages are packed in bundles and carried hop by hop until they arrive.

questions: what is custody transfer in dtn
subtitle: A store-and-forward protocol for moving bundles of data across networks with long delays and broken connections.

tldr.problem: Ordinary Internet protocols expect a connected path with short delays. Some environments have intermittent connectivity, large or variable delays and high bit error rates, so end-to-end sessions do not work.
tldr.mechanism: The Bundle Protocol (BP) sits at the application layer as a store-and-forward overlay. Data is packed into bundles made of blocks, named by endpoint IDs, and passed from node to node, optionally with custody transfer so that a node keeps a copy until another node takes over.
tldr.outcome: RFC 5050 specifies version 6 of the protocol, its block formats and its abstract service. It is Experimental, from the IRTF Delay Tolerant Networking Research Group, and not a candidate for any Internet Standard.

sections.title: Delay Tolerant Networking and the Bundle Protocol
sections.content:
RFC 5050 describes version 6 of the bundle protocol (BP) for Delay Tolerant Networking (DTN), an end-to-end architecture for stressed environments: intermittent connectivity, large or variable delays and high bit error rates. BP forms a store-and-forward overlay network at the application layer of some number of constituent internets. It uses each internet's own native protocols to move data, through a convergence layer adapter. The word internet here is used in a general sense and does not have to mean TCP/IP.

Key capabilities are custody-based retransmission, coping with intermittent connectivity, using scheduled, predicted and opportunistic connectivity as well as continuous links, and late binding of overlay endpoint identifiers to constituent internet addresses.

The document defines the format of the protocol data units, called bundles, passed between bundle nodes. It does not cover the internal workings of convergence layer adapters, the bundle routing algorithm, or how routing and forwarding tables are filled in. If BP is used on the Internet, the RFC says IETF standard protocols for security and congestion control should be used. An IESG note adds that the IETF disclaims any knowledge of the fitness of this RFC for any purpose.
sections.eli5: When the usual roads are often closed, you build a relay on top of them. Each stop keeps the package safe until the next road opens.

sections.title: Nodes, Endpoints and Registrations
sections.content:
A bundle is a sequence of two or more blocks. A bundle node is anything that can send or receive bundles, and it has three conceptual parts: a bundle protocol agent (BPA) that runs the protocol, convergence layer adapters (CLAs) that send and receive bundles over a native protocol, and an application agent (AA) that uses the service. The RFC sketches four example architectures, from a shared server to a dedicated bundle router, to show that the design does not favour one implementation.

Destinations are endpoints, sets of nodes named by an endpoint ID. An endpoint with exactly one node is a singleton, and every node must belong to at least one singleton. Sending to an endpoint can act like unicast, like anycast (any N of the nodes) or like multicast (all of them), depending on the endpoint ID. A node joins an endpoint through a registration, which is either Active (bundles are delivered automatically) or Passive, where a delivery failure action either defers delivery until polled or abandons it.

The BPA offers its application agent seven services: start a registration, end one, switch between Active and Passive, transmit a bundle, cancel a transmission, poll a Passive registration, and deliver a received bundle.
sections.eli5: Each helper has a mailbox name. Several helpers can share one name, and a helper can be told to hand over letters right away, or to keep them until someone asks.

sections.title: The Bundle Format
sections.content:
A bundle is a concatenation of at least two blocks. The first must be the single primary bundle block. At most one block may be the payload block, and the last block must have its last-block flag set to 1. Other block types can follow to support extensions such as the Bundle Security Protocol.

Nearly every number is a Self-Delimiting Numeric Value (SDNV). Each octet carries 7 bits of the value, and the top bit is 1 on every octet except the last. An N-bit value needs ceil(N/7) octets, so overhead is one bit in seven. Implementations may treat an SDNV above 264 minus 1 as invalid.

Endpoint IDs are URIs, written as a scheme name and a scheme-specific part (SSP), each at most 1023 bytes. They are stored once in a dictionary in the primary block and cited elsewhere by pairs of offsets, which compresses repeated IDs. Besides the dtn scheme, which defines the null endpoint dtn:none, any scheme registered under the URI rules may be used.

The primary block holds the version (0x06), the processing flags, destination, source, report-to and current-custodian endpoint references, a creation timestamp (time in seconds since the start of 2000 UTC, plus a sequence number), a lifetime, the dictionary and, for fragments, a fragment offset and total length. Other blocks start with a one-byte block type (1 for the payload), SDNV flags and a length. Blocks of type 192 through 255 are for private or experimental use. A node that cannot process an extension block must pass it on with the "forwarded without being processed" flag set, and must keep blocks in order.
sections.eli5: A bundle is a parcel with a label first and then the contents. Numbers on the label are written with as few digits as possible, and the names of people are written once in a list and pointed to afterwards.

sections.title: Forwarding, Expiry and Fragmentation
sections.content:
A bundle is sent in response to a transmission request from the application agent. The node adds a retention constraint, such as Dispatch pending or Forward pending, which stops the bundle from being discarded until work is done. If the destination endpoint includes the node, the bundle is delivered locally. Otherwise the BPA picks the next endpoints and the convergence layer adapters to reach them. How it chooses is outside the RFC. If no endpoint or adapter can be selected, forwarding is contraindicated, and the agent decides whether to wait or to declare forwarding failed, after which the bundle is deleted unless the node is itself the destination.

A bundle expires when the current time exceeds its creation time plus its lifetime, and must then be deleted for the reason "lifetime expired".

When a contact is too short for a whole bundle, the BPA may fragment it unless the "must not be fragmented" flag is set. A fragment keeps the source ID and creation timestamp and carries the first N or the last M - N bytes of the payload. Blocks that come before the payload go in the lowest-offset fragment, and blocks after it go in the highest. The destination reassembles the original data unit once the fragments add up to the total length.
sections.eli5: If a package will not fit through a short window of time, the helper cuts it into smaller packages. The final stop puts the pieces back together. Every package also has an expiry date after which helpers throw it away.

sections.title: Custody Transfer and Administrative Records
sections.content:
With custody transfer requested, a node that accepts custody commits to keep a copy, re-forwarding if needed, until custody is released. For singleton destinations that happens when another node accepts custody, when delivery is confirmed, or when the bundle is deleted. The procedures cover only singleton destinations. The accepting node sends a "Succeeded" custody signal to the previous custodian and updates the current-custodian ID. It may set a countdown timer, and it should keep the bundle in persistent storage if possible. If the timer runs out or a "Failed" signal arrives, the node decides what to do, for example re-forwarding over another route.

Two kinds of administrative records travel as ordinary bundles: status reports and custody signals. A status report tells the report-to endpoint when a bundle was received, had custody accepted, was forwarded, delivered or deleted, with a one-byte reason code such as lifetime expired, depleted storage or no known route to destination. Time values are DTN times: seconds since the start of 2000 plus nanoseconds. Generating reports is optional except when a bundle with custody transfer requested is deleted, because reports could add too much traffic.

Convergence layer adapters must provide two services: sending a bundle to the nodes of an endpoint's minimum reception group, and delivering to the BPA a bundle sent by a remote node.
sections.eli5: A helper can promise to look after a package until the next helper says they have it. Little notes are sent back to say that the package moved on, arrived or was thrown away.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
Security services are specified in a separate document, the Bundle Security Protocol, and this RFC only summarizes them. The concerns are that only authorized entities may consume scarce network resources, that payload integrity is preserved over long delays, and that confidentiality can be provided. Three independent security blocks are named. The Bundle Authentication Block provides hop-by-hop authenticity and integrity, the Payload Security Block gives security-source to security-destination authenticity and integrity, and the Confidentiality Block indicates the algorithm and key IDs used to encrypt the payload.

Forwarding nodes must not break bundle security, so they must not reorder blocks, and removing blocks that lack the discard-if-unprocessable flag may cause security to fail. The RFC recommends including the Bundle Security Protocol in implementations but makes its use optional.
sections.eli5: Locks and seals for parcels are described in a different paper. This one just says helpers must not shuffle the parcel in ways that spoil the seals.
